text.p: These are the headlines selected from Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Red's crest reaches Winnipeg: Water not quite so high as feared; dikes hold as muddy flood rolls through city.
- Electoral officer weighs vote delay: Kingsley to inspect flooded ridings.
- Labour evicts British Tories: Voters give Blair landslide majority.
- CRTC to allow local-phone rivalry: Cable companies, others to enter competition for customer dollars.
- Liberals woo elite in pre-election letter: Access to Chretien, cabinet ministers promised in return for $1,000 fee to join party's Laurier Club.
- CRTC rings in new telco era: Rulings clear way for cable TV, phone companies to compete in each other's markets.
- Barrick sticks to takeover strategy: Firm to target quality assets.
- Canadian dollar roars back amid rate hopes: Markets bet Fed will limit increase.
- Tobacco law won't hurt Imperial profit: Imasco.
- Phone market thrown open: New carriers free to storm local phone sector as CRTC hauls down the barriers to competition. But don't expect cheaper calls too soon.
- Trading in Bre-X shares reined in as deadline looms on Busang report.
